title: Overcast Compat Generated Test Registry
description: Machine-generated sibling of registry.json. Every loader concatenates the two; the join key (group name, test name) is shared, so a generated group may never reuse a hand-written name. Rewritten wholly by cmd/compatgen — never hand-edited. See docs/plans/compat-coverage-modelgen.md § 3.6.

ported.description: Hand-written groups an authored scenario resolves (docs/plans/compat-coverage-modelgen.md §3.11 step 3). Each names a group declared in registry.json — never one in `groups` below — and carries the one thing about it that is derived rather than decided: the suites whose scenario backend can execute it. The group's own entry, and the names every gate file keys on, stay in the hand-written registry.

group.description: The hand-written registry group this scopes. It must declare `scenario` with the same value as the entry's, and it must not also appear in `groups`.

scenario.description: The authored IR file that resolves the group, repository-relative. Cross-checked against the hand-written group's own `scenario`, so a half-applied edit cannot survive.

suites.description: Mechanically derived from backend availability, exactly as a generated group's `suites` is: the scenarioBackends table minus any suite whose emitter refused the group. A suite absent from it neither implements the group nor carries parity debt for it. An empty list would scope a group whose native implementations are being deleted to no suite at all, so it fails generation rather than being written.

GeneratedTestGroup.description: The shared TestGroup shape plus the three fields that only generated groups carry. The shape is $ref'd rather than copied: the two registries are joined on group and test names, so a second copy of the definition could drift and start accepting names the hand-written registry rejects.

generated.description: Always true. Marks the group as generator output for the dashboard facet, the report and the lint — 'which file did this come from' must never be inferred from a naming convention.

scenario.description: Path to the scenario IR file this group was generated from, relative to the repository root. Regenerating from that file must reproduce the group byte-identically; it is also how a reviewer gets from a failing test back to the recipe that produced it.

state.description: candidate = runs everywhere and reports everywhere, but gates nothing: excluded from both --compare-baseline and --max-failures. The inverse of flaky.json — quarantined by default until it proves itself, rather than gated by default until someone gets a label. gated = has passed the soak and is enforced exactly like a hand-written group.

shadowOf.description: Present only on a shadow group: the hand-written group whose native implementations this authored scenario is being compared against before they are deleted (docs/plans/compat-coverage-modelgen.md §3.11, step 2). `cmd/compat --compare-shadow` joins the two on it; `--promote-generated` skips a group that carries it, because a shadow is collecting evidence of agreement with the native group, not with itself, and is deleted when that evidence is in. A shadow group is therefore always in state "candidate".

parallel.description: The group's tests may run concurrently with one another, bounded by the suite's existing parallel-slot count (OVERCAST_COMPAT_PARALLEL_SLOTS, default 8). Emitted only on a probe group, whose tests have no setup, no teardown and no exports and so cannot order one another; a lifecycle group never carries it. Results are still collected and emitted in registry order, so honouring it changes the wall clock and nothing else. Absent means serial, which is what every loader did before the field existed and what a loader that ignores it still does.

suites.description: Mechanically derived from backend availability by cmd/compatgen, never hand-edited. A suite absent from this list neither implements the group nor carries parity debt for it — which is what keeps a model refresh from inflating debt for six suites that were never asked to run the tests.
